name: Shopify customer accounts (passwordless)
evidence: Read-only DOM read on 2026-09-21 against account.colourpop.com, reached from colourpop.com/account, which served /authentication/login. The email input matched exactly one visible element; both submit buttons were confirmed to belong to the email's own form. Nothing was typed or submitted.
gotchas: Passwordless: completing this signup needs the code emailed to the account owner. There is no step a vault password can fill.

The aria-label 'Continue' is English, so on a translated store use the fallback, which keys on the PRESENCE of aria-label rather than its text. It names the same button alone. Do not drop the [aria-label] from it: the email's form holds a second submit, labelled 'Submit', and a selector matching both cannot be clicked under strict locator semantics.
The form id (FormP0-17 when observed) and the hashed classes are generated per build. Do not target them.

Nothing in this flow's URL is unique to Shopify: it runs on the store's own account.<store> subdomain, and /authentication/login is a generic path. So it has no URL detect signal at all and is reached only through a host-keyed signup recipe naming this platform. Inferring it from the path would hand these selectors to unrelated login pages.
notes: Shopify's newer customer accounts are passwordless, with one page for signing in and signing up. Entering an email sends a one-time code, and entering that code creates the account if none exists. There is no password field in the flow, so a vault-minted password is never used here.

steps.open: Open /account on the store's domain. A store on these accounts redirects to a Shopify-hosted page, observed at account.<store>/authentication/login.
steps.fill: Fill #customer-authentication-web-email with the email token. The input has no name attribute.
steps.submit: Click the 'Continue' arrow beside the email field.
steps.verify: Shopify emails a one-time code to the address. That code belongs to the account owner: hand off to them, and never guess or automate it.
